title: What The Banjo Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 105bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Appalachian Celtic philosophy absurdist
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The banjo arrived in America from West Africa originally
Which surprises people who assume it's exclusively hillbilly
The five-string banjo in the mountains of Appalachia
Developed its own dialect and chose to stay right there

[Pre-Chorus]
I heard one at a bluegrass festival in the rain
I ran toward it and then away from it and then back again

[Chorus]
What does the banjo know that I don't know?
It knows the shortest distance between Africa and Carolina's flow
What does the banjo know on the mountain side?
It knows that music travels further than the people who supplied
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The clawhammer style is one technique, the three-finger is another
Both are valid and both players will tell you that the other
Is technically inferior — this is a tradition too
The banjo knows that argument is part of what it grew into

[Bridge]
There's a banjo in an Irish session somewhere right now
Playing reels beside a fiddle and nobody questions how
The banjo crossed the Atlantic and came back by a different door
The banjo knows that music has no passport at its core

[Outro]
Banjo knows… Africa to Appalachia to Ireland… banjo knows
That's my boy
